manifest.name: Workloads
manifest.description: Browse and operate Kubernetes resources: pods, deployments, services, nodes and every built-in kind.

deletePod.title: Delete Pod {{name}}?
deletePod.message: The Pod is deleted. If a controller such as a Deployment owns it, the controller replaces it with a new one.

buttons.newHint: Create a {{kind}} or any other resource from a template or a file

delete.title: Delete {{kind}} {{name}}?
delete.messageCluster: The {{kind}} {{name}} is deleted from the cluster. It is cluster-scoped, so its name has to be typed.

policyHelp.background: It disappears at once; Kubernetes then deletes the objects it owns in the background.
policyHelp.foreground: It stays, marked for deletion, until every object it owns is deleted; then it disappears too.
policyHelp.orphan: Only it is deleted. The objects it owns keep running without an owner.

delete.cascadeOrphan: Nothing cascades: {{chain}} would otherwise be deleted with it.

metadata.title: Labels and annotations of {{kind}} {{name}}
metadata.description: Only what you change is sent; keys you remove are deleted from the object.
metadata.lastAppliedKept: kubectl's last-applied-configuration annotation is not shown and stays as it is.
metadata.keyInvalid: A key has at most one "/": an optional prefix, then a name.
metadata.prefixInvalid: The prefix must be a DNS subdomain such as example.com (lower case, at most 253 characters).
metadata.nameInvalid: The name must be at most 63 letters, digits, "-", "_" or ".", starting and ending with a letter or digit.
metadata.valueInvalid: The value of label {{key}} must be empty or at most 63 letters, digits, "-", "_" or ".", starting and ending with a letter or digit.

reveal.title: Reveal the values of Secret {{name}}?
reveal.warning: The values are shown in plain text, here only, and are not kept once you close this dialog. Revealing is recorded in the audit log. Make sure nobody is looking over your shoulder.
reveal.shown: These are the Secret's real values. They are gone when you close this dialog.
reveal.copyBase64: Copy the value of {{key}} as base64

node.cordoned: Node {{name}} cordoned: no new Pods are scheduled on it.
node.uncordoned: Node {{name}} uncordoned: Pods can be scheduled on it again.
node.noTaints: No taints: Pods without tolerations can run here.

drain.title: Drain node {{name}}?
drain.message: The node is cordoned, then its Pods are evicted through the eviction API. PodDisruptionBudgets are respected: a Pod one of them protects stays until the budget allows the eviction or the timeout ends.
drain.ignoreDaemonSetsHelp: Leave them on the node. Without this, their presence stops the drain.
drain.deleteEmptyDirDataHelp: Also evict Pods with emptyDir volumes; their data is lost.
drain.forceHelp: Also evict Pods that no controller manages; nothing recreates them.
drain.gracePeriodHelp: How long each Pod may take to stop.
drain.gracePeriodInvalid: Enter whole seconds from 0 to {{max}}, or leave it empty.
drain.timeoutHelp: Pods still on the node by then are reported.
drain.cordonedNote: The node stays cordoned; uncordon it to schedule Pods on it again.
drain.nothing: No Pods had to leave the node.
drain.errorsHint: Change the options to cover these Pods, then drain again.
drain.blockedHint: Their budget allowed no further disruption before the timeout. Add replicas on other nodes or wait, then drain again.

taints.title: Taints of node {{name}}
taints.description: A taint keeps Pods off the node unless they tolerate it. Saving replaces all taints of the node.
taints.heading: Taints ({{count}})
taints.empty: No taints. Add one, or save to remove them all.
taints.duplicate: This key already has a taint with this effect.
taints.noExecuteWarning: NoExecute also evicts the running Pods that do not tolerate the taint.

rollout.loadFailed: Could not load the rollout history
rollout.pausedReason: The rollout is paused; resume it to roll back.
rollout.pausedNote: The rollout is paused: changes to the Pod template wait until it is resumed, and it cannot be rolled back.
rollout.rollbackMessage: The Deployment gets the Pod template of revision {{revision}} ({{images}}) back and replaces its Pods following its update strategy. The rollback becomes a new revision.

workload.replicasInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {{max}}.
workload.managedBy: {{owner}} manages this object and will undo the change; scale it instead.

pods.forceDeleteMessage: The Pod is removed at once, without waiting for its containers to stop. The node may keep them running for a while, and a StatefulSet may start the replacement while the old Pod still runs.
pods.deleteTooMany: {{count}} Pods are selected; one delete takes at most {{max}}. Narrow the selection, e.g. with the filter.
pods.bulkMessage: Pods a controller owns are replaced by new ones.
pods.bulkForceHelp: Remove the Pods at once, without waiting for their containers to stop.

debug.title: Debug Pod {{name}}
debug.description: Adds an ephemeral container with a shell to the running Pod and opens a terminal in it. Ephemeral containers cannot be removed: this one stays until the Pod is deleted.
debug.imageHelp: The image needs a shell. Empty: {{image}}.
debug.invalidImage: An image reference contains no spaces.
debug.targetHelp: The debug container sees the processes of this container.
debug.starting: Starting the debug container. The shell opens once it runs; pulling its image can take up to a minute.

namespace.name: Name
namespace.nameHelp: Lower-case letters, digits and -, at most 63 characters.
namespace.deleteMessage: The namespace and everything in it, workloads, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets and volume claims included, are deleted. This cannot be undone.
namespace.systemReason: Kubernetes needs its system namespaces; KubeBench does not delete them.
namespace.forceHelp: Ignore KubeBench's protection of this namespace and delete it.

validation.namespaceName: Use lower-case letters, digits and -, starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters.
validation.qualifiedName: Use a name like dedicated or example.com/zone: letters, digits, -, _ and ., at most 63 characters, with an optional DNS prefix.
validation.labelValue: At most 63 letters, digits, -, _ and ., starting and ending with a letter or digit.
